newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Acacia sees A$19 mln half year net profit.
newsitem.headline: Acacia sees A$19 mln half year net profit.

text.p: Gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd said on Thursday it expected its net profit after abnormals for the half year to June 30 to rise to about A$19 million, compared with A$7.5 million a year ago.
Acacia said its half year net profit before abnormals was expected to be about A$13 million, with an abnormal profit after tax of about A$6 million.
Acacia's half year results are due to be released August 7.
Acacia said the higher net profit was expected to reflect lower operating costs and the favourable impact of the first full quarter's production from Sunrise dam.
It said that at June 30, its net debt position was A$32.2 million, compared wtih A$63.6 million at the end of March.

"This reflects the impact of the completion of construction of the Sunrise Dam gold mine, the first full quarter's operating cashflow from Sunrise Dam, and A$27 million cash proceeds from the completion of the sale of Blendevale in June 1997," it said.

Acacia said that during the June quarter, 112,983 ounces of gold were sold at an average net realised price of A$575 per ounce, representing a premium of A$129 per ounces, or 29 percent above the quarter's average sport price of A$46.

During the first half of 1997, 179,428 ounces of gold were sold at an average net realised gold price of A$585 per ounce, a premium of A$136 per ounce above the average spot price of A$49 for the period.
"All forecast production to the end of 1998 and the equivalent of a further 2.5 years' production, at current production levels, has been hedged," Acacia said in its June quarter production report.
Forward sales and put options represented hedging of 77 percent of reserves being mined or 55 percent of all reserves.
